# Results — Study 45 (Vanishing-Act): the size premium across the longest free proxies

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Monthly total returns of three size
pairs (Yahoo): **^RUT − ^GSPC** (Russell 2000 vs S&P 500, 1987–2026 — the long history) and the
total-return ETF pairs **IWM − SPY** and **IJR − IVV** (2000–2026). SMB = small − large. Inputs
fingerprint `da49197bc37d`.*

## The verdict, earned — Signal `NONE` · Tradability `MIRAGE` · "Survived publication"? `BUSTED`

The size premium is finance's original factor (Banz 1981) — and, on the longest free proxy, it is
**gone**. Russell 2000 minus S&P 500 over **39 years** earns **+0.1%/yr at a Sharpe of 0.01 (Lo t =
0.05)** — indistinguishable from zero — and small-caps actually **trail** large-caps risk-adjusted
(Sharpe 0.47 vs 0.61). The same on the tradable ETF pairs: SMB is statistically insignificant (Lo t
0.5–1.1). And the decay is `BUSTED`-clear and consistent across all three pairs: **positive before 2010,
negative since.** The premium that defined the small-cap fund industry worked until it was published.

## Data stamp

- **Long history**: ^RUT − ^GSPC, 1987-10 → 2026-06, 465 months
- **Tradable**: IWM − SPY and IJR − IVV total return, 2000–2026, 313 months — fingerprint `da49197bc37d`

## The premium is statistically zero — and small-caps lose on Sharpe

| pair | SMB mean/yr | SMB Sharpe | Lo t | small Sharpe | large Sharpe |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ^RUT − ^GSPC (1987–2026) | **+0.1%** | **0.01** | **0.05** | 0.47 | 0.61 |
| IWM − SPY (2000–2026) | +1.0% | 0.10 | 0.50 | 0.51 | 0.76 |
| IJR − IVV (2000–2026) | +2.1% | 0.21 | 1.05 | 0.58 | 0.60 |

Not one pair clears |t| = 2. On the longest series the spread is *zero*, and small-caps deliver a
*lower* Sharpe than large-caps — the opposite of a risk-adjusted premium. The S&P 600 pair (IJR, which
screens for profitability) does marginally best, hinting the surviving "size" edge is really a **quality
screen**, not size.

## …and it reversed after it was published

| | ^RUT − ^GSPC | IWM − SPY | IJR − IVV |
|---|---|---|---|
| pre-2010 SMB (mean/yr) | **+1.1%** | **+5.7%** | **+7.7%** |
| 2010-on SMB (mean/yr) | **−1.3%** | **−1.8%** | **−1.1%** |

Every pair tells the same story: a positive size premium in the earlier decades, **negative since
2010**. Banz documented the effect in 1981; by the modern era it has not merely faded but **changed
sign** — the cleanest McLean–Pontiff post-publication decay in the whole bench.

## The honest takeaway

The size premium — the factor that launched a thousand small-cap funds — is a `MIRAGE` today: zero over
39 years, small-caps trailing large on Sharpe, and a clean sign reversal since 2010. What little edge
survives in the S&P 600 pair looks like a quality screen wearing a size label. `NONE` on the spread,
`MIRAGE` to trade, the survived-publication claim `BUSTED`.
